L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and

a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: Measured absolute or systemic oral bioavailability in structurally related opioid contexts is consistently above the 20% threshold: meptazinol 27.9% in cirrhotic patients (C08), pentazocine 0.68–0.70 in cirrhosis (C07, C11), codeine 80.5% in healthy subjects (C04), and pethidine 0.80 ± 0.15 in cirrhosis (C10, C14).
The query is a rigid morphinan opioid (hydromorphone-like) sharing the phenolic morphinan scaffold with codeine and naloxegol; no visible L1 record for a close opioid analogue reports F below 20%.

Naloxegol, an opioid-derived morphinan, had simulated absolute oral bioavailability of 0.90 (C02), providing additional but less direct support for high oral bioavailability of the morphinan scaffold.

evidence_gaps: No direct hydromorphone absolute oral bioavailability record is present in the visible L1 set.
No affirmative F <20% record for a close opioid analogue is present; the lowest relevant positive is meptazinol at 27.9%.

Several opioid records were obtained in cirrhosis patients, a condition that can alter first-pass metabolism; the direction remains positive but exact quantitative transfer to healthy hydromorphone is uncertain.
No dose-, formulation-, or prandial-state-matched hydromorphone data are available.
content.decision_summary: All visible L1 records with relevant opioid scaffolds report F above 20% (meptazinol 27.9%, pentazocine 68–70%, codeine 80.5%, pethidine 80%, naloxegol 90%); the query is a morphinan opioid structurally related to these contexts, and no affirmative evidence supports F <20%. Therefore predict high with moderate confidence.
